newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia orders probe into sensitive contract bid.
newsitem.headline: Colombia orders probe into sensitive contract bid.

text.p: Investigators opened a preliminary inquiry on Thursday into alleged irregularities in the bidding process for a contract to modernize Colombia's civil register, the chief prosecutor's office said.

German multinational Siemens emerged as the frontrunner for the contract, estimated to be worth more than $90 million, although heads of the National Civil Register Office have not yet formally named a winner.

Unisys, of the United States, and Sofremi, of France, were also competing for the contract. The government has refused to release details of the bidding process on the grounds it was a senstive national security issue.

"The chief prosecutor has ordered a preliminary investigation into the bidding process for the civil register contract. The inquiry will be conducted by a commission of regional prosecutors," a spokesman for the chief prosecutor's office said.

Allegations of irregularities in the bidding process emerged after German private detective Werner Mauss was arrested in the city of Medellin almost two weeks ago as he tried to smuggle a rebel kidnap victim out the country.
Siemens said it had previously used Mauss as an unofficial intermediary to break the deadlock over an unfinished contract to build the Medellin Metro in the early 1990s.

In a press release issued late Wednesday Siemens said, "We reject false arguments that seek to disqualify Siemens' bid, which was rated as the best by the only body responsible for making an objective selection."
